definitions.explanation: Meat that has been finely chopped or ground. From English 'mince.' Used in cooking contexts, particularly in the Kansai region.

examples.japanese: ⟦{豚|ぶた}→豚：04710_buta⟧ミンチ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧200⟦グラム→グラム：01354_guramu⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought 200 grams of ground pork.

examples.japanese: ミンチ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦ハンバーグ→ハンバーグ：01785_hanbaagu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I'll make hamburger steaks using ground meat.

examples.japanese: {合|あい}い{挽|び}きミンチ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}→牛肉：02874_gyuuniku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{豚肉|ぶたにく}→豚肉：02956_butaniku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{混|ま}ぜた→混ぜる：02423_mazeru⟧{挽|ひ}き{肉|にく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ことだ。
examples.english: Mixed ground meat is ground meat that combines beef and pork.

notes:
From English "mince." Used especially in the Kansai region. In the Kanto region and standard Japanese, {挽|ひ}き{肉|にく} (ground meat) is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{豚|ぶた}→豚：04710_buta⟧ミンチ: ground pork
- {牛|ぎゅう}ミンチ: ground beef
- {鶏|とり}ミンチ: ground chicken
- {合|あい}い{挽|び}きミンチ: mixed ground meat (beef and pork)
- ミンチカツ: minced meat cutlet (a Kansai specialty)

REGIONAL DIFFERENCE:
- ミンチ: predominantly Kansai region
- {挽|ひ}き{肉|にく}: standard Japanese and Kanto region

Both words refer to the same product, and either will be understood anywhere in Japan. However, supermarket labels tend to follow regional conventions.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {挽|ひ}き{肉|にく}: ground meat — the standard Japanese term
- ⟦ひき{肉|にく}→ひき肉：17241_hikiniku⟧: ground meat — same word written without kanji for {挽|ひ}き
